a-sigkill.interpretation: Native generation accounted for 6,000 events; 21 are absent from both the durable queue and Sentinel around the forced-kill boundary. All 5,979 accepted identities reached Sentinel. The exact loss location before durable admission has not been conclusively established; do not relabel this as a passing native-to-destination test.

transportAssessment.protocol: rsyslog omfwd TCP/TLS syslog without application acknowledgement
transportAssessment.durableAdmissionReview: The decoded frame awaits the sink, processor and SQLite commit before internal queued success returns. No application acknowledgement is transmitted on the syslog connection.
transportAssessment.receiveBoundary: TCP/TLS transport and bounded reader buffers can acknowledge or retain bytes before durable application admission. ResendLastMSGOnReconnect cannot identify an arbitrary uncommitted tail.
transportAssessment.conclusion: Observed native-to-destination failure with complete admitted-to-destination identity delivery. The precise socket/TLS/reader loss location is not proven.
transportAssessment.requiredForCrashLosslessClaim: Application-acknowledged ingestion or retained-source replay with independently qualified recovery.

limitations: Each passing phase qualifies only its exact recorded scope. Retained native completeness failures (a-reset, a-sender-reboot, a-sigkill) prevent a lossless native firewall-to-destination claim; general production readiness is not established.
Sampler completeness is resource evidence only and does not establish destination delivery.
The original Windows smoke failed all five metric samples under PS5.1 and is preserved. The fixed run passed all five. A separate premature export of the fixed run is recorded independently.
report.png is a screenshot of this local rendered HTML evidence summary, not an AWS/Azure portal capture.

preflightFailures.cause: The probe assumed every deployment output was an ARM value object, but the retained state also contains flattened output values.
preflightFailures.evidence: The second attempt's sanitized traceback identifies the output-normalization comprehension at line 43, before cache creation or any ingestion request. The first attempt returned the same exception category before this diagnostic was added.
preflightFailures.correction: Normalize dictionary value objects and already-flattened outputs before endpoint validation.

monitoring.scope: Malformed-request diagnostics are independent of collector delivery; TLS alerts are baseline expiry/missing-CRL coverage. Only the two explicitly bounded query results are alert-window proof.

originalAlertRecovery.scope: Original Linux destination-outage health alert plus original DCR metric/log diagnostic alerts only. Later Windows and synthetic probe alerts are separate; this is not an all-alerts-clear claim.

laterAlertRecovery.scope: Three exact observed alert IDs only; rule/start identity matches are verified. This does not attribute a multi-collector rule to a specific host or establish a global all-clear.

latestDeployedWindowQueries.interpretation: Both real collectors are absent from health-missing. The Windows backlog row has zero current pending and idle delivery; its PT30M maximum arrival lag remains 15.4 minutes. Synthetic health and disposable TLS conditions remain separate; no all-alerts-clear claim.

finalSnapshot.scope: Final owned alert metadata and exact deployed query windows; synthetic probes, disposable TLS baselines and retired-host alerts are distinct scopes.

windows.remainingScope: Linux/Sender instances and their main stack, retained S3 bucket and Azure validation resources remain until Linux testing finishes.

limitations: This is not an account-wide all-region billing audit.
Stack deletion covers stack-owned route associations; shared VPC/NAT infrastructure is intentionally preserved.
Private staging-file removal is verified separately.
